name: Build and release controls, one chapter per OWASP Top 10 CI/CD Security Risk
source: Written for this skill. The chapters follow the risk list of https://owasp.org/www-project-top-10-ci-cd-security-risks/; no OWASP text is copied.
license: MIT, as the rest of this repository

requirements.text: A change reaches the default branch or a release branch only through a reviewed pull request; no workflow, bot or person pushes to it without review.
A release or production deployment runs only from a protected branch or a protected tag, and needs an approval or a protected environment.

requirements.chapter: C2 Identity and access in the pipeline (CICD-SEC-2)
requirements.section: C2 Identity and access in the pipeline (CICD-SEC-2)
requirements.text: Every workflow and job declares the least token permissions it needs (for example `permissions:` in GitHub Actions) and does not rely on a default token that can write.

requirements.chapter: C2 Identity and access in the pipeline (CICD-SEC-2)
requirements.section: C2 Identity and access in the pipeline (CICD-SEC-2)
requirements.text: Each identity the pipeline uses (a deploy key, a service account, a cloud role) is scoped to the one repository, environment and action it serves.
Every build installs dependencies from a lockfile with exact versions and integrity hashes, and runs package install scripts only where they were reviewed.
Package sources are named explicitly, so that an internal package name can never be resolved from a public registry.

Code from a pull request, a fork or a comment never runs in a job that holds secrets or a token that can write; triggers such as `pull_request_target`, `workflow_run` and comment commands check out only trusted code.

Values an outsider controls (branch names, pull request titles and bodies, commit messages, issue text) never reach a shell, a script or an expression without quoting, for example through an environment variable.
Each job can reach only the secrets, environments, cloud roles and network it needs, and production credentials are available only to a protected environment.
No credential is committed to the repository or written into a workflow, a build file, an image layer or a log.

The pipeline authenticates to clouds and registries with short-lived federated credentials (OIDC) instead of long-lived keys, and each trust policy names the repository and the branch or environment it trusts.
Self-hosted runners are ephemeral or isolated per job, and do not run jobs for pull requests from outside the repository.
Caches and artifacts written by untrusted jobs (pull requests) are never read by trusted jobs (release, deploy).
Every third-party action, orb, plugin or reusable workflow is pinned to a full commit SHA or a digest, not to a tag or a branch.
Third-party apps and integrations with access to the repository or the pipeline are listed with the permissions they hold, and none holds more than its use needs.
Base images and downloaded tools are pinned by digest or checksum and verified before use; no script is piped from the network into a shell.
Published artifacts (packages, images, release files) are signed or carry provenance that a consumer can verify.
Pipeline runs, approvals and changes to pipeline configuration are logged where the owner can review them, and secrets are masked in job logs.
